findings.title: Unchecked service connection options survive validation and reach Pool
findings.repro: Run python3 review-r1/run-probe.py service-extra-fields-private.mjs. Existing recorded run exits0. Exact service accepts; wrong-host rejects; extra connectionString targeting a different endpoint/user accepts; same-endpoint connectionString using admin pare224 instead of assigned service role accepts; extra ssl accepts. Probe invokes frozen W helper with virtual fs through Node22 module hooks only. No PG dependency, app body, Docker, child or connection is invoked.
findings.expected: Reject connection-authority options outside the finite six-field service contract, or supply only the validated six fields downstream. The exact checked object should be used rather than re-reading unprojected JSON.
findings.observed: assignedService checks selected fields but ignores other keys. Consumer service() reads and returns the full JSON as Connection (a TypeScript assertion does not remove fields). new Pool({...conn,...}) forwards unchecked connectionString/ssl.
findings.impact: A private service descriptor that passes the assignment guard can carry a second connection authority contradicting its verified host/port/database/role/options. ConnectionString override behavior is the downstream node-postgres API implication; an actual effective PG connection was deliberately not run. Guard acceptance and full-object forwarding are directly demonstrated/static, respectively.
findings.missingProof: No negative test covers alternate connection-authority fields or proves the final effective Pool connection remains identical to the assignment. Passing current33 helper tests does not close this hole.
